title: Karl Eberhards Corpus of spontaneously spoken southern German in dialogues
why_promising: Primary spontaneous Southern German dialogue corpus. Current University of Tübingen documentation reports 40 dialogues, separate audio channels, about half an hour of articulography for 20 speakers, Praat annotations, and manually corrected word boundaries; the associated corpus paper states that word-level TextGrids were manually corrected and segment-level boundaries were then forced-aligned within those corrected word boundaries. This gives an isolatable human-grounded temporal layer plus primary audio and EMA trajectories.
open_question: Resolve the BAS/CLARIN KEC distribution at file level and enumerate downloadable WAV, TextGrid, EMA, questionnaire and script objects, checksums, access terms and redistribution license. Admit manual word intervals but keep automatically aligned segment boundaries explicitly outside the manual core unless independently human-corrected.
